title: Yost's hat trick paces Bucs
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Yost's hat trick paces Bucs

 September 26, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 700
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — It took Kent Island High's field hockey team some time to adjust to life without graduated standout Megan Carpenter last year.Without Carpenter — who was seemingly everywhere on the field — the Bucs dropped their first three games, and were outscored 8-7 through their opening five games.
That has not been the case this season.
Kent Island showed its strength on offense, defense and at the midfield Thursday, as Willow Yost notched her first hat trick of the season and Ellie Burnside totaled three assists to fuel a 4-1 victory over Crisfield at Andy Schipul Stadium.
"We don't really have a superstar," Bucs head coach Laura Harding said after her team improved to 4-1. "We are a very, very balanced team. And I think last year we lost Megan and it took us a little while to figure it out because she did everything for us. She was on defense. She was on offense. She was distributing the ball all over the field. Everywhere.
"So it just took us a little while last year to figure it out, which is why I think we were way stronger at the end of the year," added Harding of a team that won eight of its last 11 games. "And we have a lot of girls on this team that play year round."
Harding may have felt she was watching last year's slow start during Thursday's first half, as the Buccaneers and Crabbers (3-2) were tied at 1-1.
"I just felt like we were a little flat in the first half and it just took us a while to get going," Harding said. "Yes, we have a very strong mid(field) and a very strong D. So that's nice. But then we just have to work on getting it in the cage, which we did the rest of the game. We were just flat in the beginning."
Yost gave Kent Island a 1-0 lead with 55 seconds remaining in the first quarter, when she scored off Sadie Latchaw's assist. Crisfield struggled to get the ball past Kent Island's midfield through the first quarter and into the second. But with 3:43 left in the half, Emily Engle set up Mya Pendry's tying goal off a corner.
"That was a beautiful goal that Crisfield had on that corner," Harding said. "The passing was gorgeous. So kudos to them."
Just a 1:20 later though, Parker Tengwall scored off the first of Burnside's three assists. Tengwall just missed giving Kent Island a two-goal halftime lead when she clanged a shot off the left post with less than a minute left in the half.
The Bucs had three corner opportunities to the Crabbers' two in the third quarter, before Burnside set up Yost's second goal for a 3-1 lead with 5:08 to go in the third.
"We kept turning over the ball and we kept passing it to the other team," Yost said of Kent Island's early struggles. "But then after the first half we definitely connected better."
The Burnside-to-Yost combination connected again with a little over 9 minutes remaining off a corner that widened Kent Island's cushion to 4-1.
"I definitely think her being in an offensive mid and me in the center, it works really well together," Yost said of her scoring connection with Burnside.
Yost thought there was a tendency for the Bucs to crowd one side of the field last season instead of spreading out. That appears to have been fixed this early season, as the Bucs have outscored their first five opponents, 13-3.
"I think we have a couple things to clean up," Harding said. "We've been working on both circles. Like I don't think that goal should have happened. And I don't the one against Parkside should have happened. So we have to work.
"But the middle of our field is solid," Harding continued. "We just have to work on finishing on the offensive end and not letting those goals in. But way better start than last year."
QUEEN ANNE'S 4 J.M. BENNETT 1CENTREVILLE — Aly Edwards had one goal and an assist, and goalie Cassidy Alexander stopped two shots as the Lions won their fourth straight.
Haley Cole, Jamie Baldwin and Jolie Leager had one goal apiece for Queen Anne's (4-1) and Ava Fields had an assist.

title: Queen Anne's outlasts Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's outlasts Easton

 October 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 897
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Queen Anne's County High's field hockey team doesn't have a goalie competition.It has a goalie luxury.
Longtime head coach Shana Corder can rotate senior Cassidy Alexander and junior Caroline Kimball throughout regulation play. But when it comes to defending a penalty stroke, Alexander draws the assignment. And when the game pushes into one vs. one play, Kimball knows it's her turn to step into the cage.
Ellee McLean and Jordan Bilbo each scored on their one vs. one chances, and Kimball allowed Easton nothing on four opportunities Tuesday afternoon, boosting Queen Anne's to a 1-0 victory over the Warriors in a game that felt more like a Class 2A regional playoff clash.
"It was a great game," said Easton head coach Kim Neff, after her team slipped to 4-3 overall, 1-1 North Bayside.
It was a game that featured strong defensive play by both teams, and huge stops by goalies on both sides.
Queen Anne's (6-1, 3-0), which hasn't lost since losing a one vs. one showdown at Pocomoke to open the season, rotated their goalies during regulation play, with Alexander playing the first and third quarters, and Kimball the second and fourth.
Alexander, registered her 100th career save with 7 minutes, 25 seconds remaining in the third quarter, when she dove to her left to smother a shot on an Easton penalty corner. Just 33 seconds later, Alexander laid flat out to foil another Warrior scoring bid, to keep the game a scoreless stalemate.
"I just thought about my team," said Alexander, when asked if save No. 100 was weighing on her mind. "We have an extremely intense team and they always are willing to give 110 percent. So when it comes to my end, it's just my job to pick up the scraps and do my job to help us win that game. And I think I definitely played a part in that."
Alexander, who finished with eight saves, played both 10-minute overtime periods, and foiled Easton's Addie Knox on the doorstep 1:38 into the first OT.
Just a freshman, Easton goalie Taylor Bowen turned away everything that came her way, and produced her biggest save at the end of the second overtime, when she denied McLean in the closing seconds.
"She is incredible," Neff said of Bowen, who finished with four saves. "Her footwork. She's really fast. She can see the field. She's great at communicating with her defense. And for a freshman who just came into the position, we're very impressed."
The game remained scoreless after two overtimes, pushing the game into one vs. one play. Each team selected five players, with each one having 10 seconds to try and score.
Kimball, who did not register a save in regulation, made three one vs. one stops, charging from the cage, flopping onto the ground while waving her stick to make deflections and foil every Easton attempt.
"She's more dynamic that me," Alexander said of Kimball when it comes to one vs. ones. "She's really good at just staying with the girl. She's incredible. She's like my little sister. I always had trust in her."
The first shooter in the game's deciding segment, McLean moved toward Bowen, stopped and made a quick circle before sending a shot into the right corner of the cage for the game's first goal.
Olivia Orrell's was Easton's first shooter, but with Kimball coming out to challenge her, never got a shot off in the 10-second limit.
Jordan Bilbo gave Queen Anne's a 2-0 lead when she steered another ball into the right side of the cage.
Kimball again came out to cut down the angle on Easton's No. 2 shooter, Maedy Leitzer, who could not find the cage.
"Definitely not my first shootout," Kimball said. "Whenever I do go into something like that I really just try to focus on what's happening in front of me. And just like, try and see what I can do to like counteract what they're trying to do. Fortunately, they had a couple of balls come at me, and that's when I swiped it away or kicked it. That was me counteracting. Most of the time I just trying to run down the time so that they have less time to score."
Queen Anne's last two shooters, Haley Cole and Ava Fields, were unable to cushion the Lions' advantage. But Kimball dove to her left to deflect Myka Motovidlak's bid, then flopped to her left again to get a piece of Addie Knox's shot, that skidded left of the cage, bringing Queen Anne's players onto the field to mob Kimball.
"Caroline knows she's our shootout goalie," Corder said. "Cassidy is better at saving strokes and Caroline is better at one v. ones. And these two girls work so well together. So Cassidy's like, 'Yes, put her in (in one v. ones). She's better at that.' So if I get a stroke call and Cassidy's on the sideline, I sub my goalie in because Cassidy's better. I'm so blessed that I have the ability to do that off the bench. In my career, that's never happened.
"And it makes the girls believe in both of them," Corder continued. "So they're confident no matter who's back there. Whether it's Cassidy the first half and then Caroline, they're totally confident with their goalies. Both are excellent leaders back there. I just couldn't be more proud of them because honestly they're literally keeping us in it."
Queen Anne's finished with 11 corners to Easton's 10.

title: Orrell's overtime goal lifts Warriors over Kent Island in thriller
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Orrell's overtime goal lifts Warriors over Kent Island in thriller

 October 15, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 730
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — Addie Knox paused.Easton High's sophomore midfielder stood on the end line 4 minutes deep into overtime preparing to deliver an entry pass on a penalty corner, when she asked her teammates aligned inside the circle's fringe, "What are we doing?"
Less than a moment later, Knox had her answer: scoring.
Olivia Orrell scored from just inside the circle Monday night, lifting Easton High's field hockey team to a 1-0 victory over Kent Island at Andy Schipul Stadium — the Warriors' second overtime win in four days.
After Tuesday's games, Queen Anne's (9-1 overall, 4-0 North Bayside) sits atop the division alone in first with Easton (7-3, 3-1) in second and Kent Island (8-3, 3-1) in third. Kent Island could forge a three-way tie atop the North when it hosts Queen Anne's Saturday. But the Lions would likely win the tiebreaker based on a better overall winning percentage.
Four days after defeating Pocomoke in overtime, Easton and the Bucs needed extra time to settle things, courtesy of some outstanding defense and fine goalie play. Warrior goalie Taylor Bowen (seven saves) faced her heaviest pressure in the first half but let nothing get by her. Easton dominated play in the second half, but couldn't beat Bucs goalie Brynja Petursson (11 saves), who stopped shots sitting and laying down, sending the scoreless stalemate into overtime.
"She's a great goalie," Kent Island head coach Laura Harding said of Petursson. "I thought the defense played well. Emma Fleshman stepped up; she was the one playing over Sydney Riska (who was out of town) and did a good job.
"We had many opportunities to put it in in the first half," Harding continued. "That's when we had the momentum and couldn't finish. You've got to finish to win."
Easton controlled the second half, and was inches from taking the lead on a corner with 7 minutes left in the third period. But Petursson, with the Warriors poking and trying to jam the ball past her, first made stops while seated, then stretched her body across the goalmouth to keep the game scoreless.
"First quarter when they came out I told them we're playing as individuals," Easton head coach Kim Neff said of her team. "And then they started communicating better and playing as a unit. That's when we kind of took over and dominated. But I have to give it to their defense and their goalie because they played a heckuva game. They are hard to get through."
Easton also got some big defensive plays. Stella Kabler poke checked the ball away from Kent Island's Rita Yost on a breakaway, and Myka Motovidlak twice spoiled threats.
Kent Island earned two late corners in the final 2 minutes of regulation, but fired wide of the cage, then watched Easton clear the second attempt, sending the game into the 7-on-7 overtime.
"I think we were really determined to get the corner, or at least get the shot off," Orrell said. "We just kept pounding the goal and I got the corner."
Knox set up on the end line to the left of Petursson and directed a pass to Orrell, who took possession, stepped out of the circle, then back in, and smacked a low, hard shot that slid past the right leg of the Bucs' goalie for the game-winner.
"I'm like, 'I can do this,'" Orrell said of the corner. "I knew it was a good shot. It was a hard hit. And then it went in and made the best sound ever. And then when the ref called it I looked at Addie and the whole team and I was so excited."
Within seconds, Orrell swarmed on by her jubilant teammates.
"It was a great game," Harding said. "Great reffed game. Great played game. Easton ended up wanting it a little more than us in the end. It was clear."
KENT ISLAND 3 KENT COUNTY 1
WORTON — Rita Yost, Caroline Levin and Audrey Fleshman each scored one goal Tuesday, as the Bucs topped the Trojans.
Ellie Burnside had an assist for Kent Island and Brynja Petursson had three saves.
QUEEN ANNE'S 7 ST. MICHAELS 0
CENTREVILLE — Ella Rebstock and Jamie Baldwin netted two goals apiece as the Lions won their ninth straight.
Jordan Bilbo and Haley Cole each had a goal and an assist for Queen Anne's. Aly Edwards added a goal and Ellee McLean an assist. The Lions didn't allow a shot on goal in posting their sixth shutout of the season.

title: Webb, Stepp score late, lift Sabres over Herons for third straight title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Webb, Stepp score late, lift Sabres over Herons for third straight title

 October 17, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 824
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — It had gone undefeated in conference play this season, outscoring its six opponents by a 58-1 margin.So it was easy to think Thursday's Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference title game was a mere gimme for Saints Peter and Paul High's field hockey team.
It was anything but.
The two-time defending champ was in a scoreless stalemate at halftime. It nudged ahead in the third, only to be tied 55 seconds into the fourth quarter. But Angie Webb and Jules Stepp scored a little more than 2 minutes apart down the stretch to give the Sabres a 3-1 victory over a stubborn Gunston squad for its third consecutive ESIAC championship.
"They came to play," Sts. Peter & Paul head coach Debbie McQuaid said of the Herons, who lost both regular-season games to the Sabres by a combined 11-1 score. "We knew it was going to be hard. Gunston's gotten better. We've gotten better. Both teams have been playing some out-of-conference strong teams. So I expected them to come at me with all they had. And they did."
Despite having a 5-1 advantage in penalty corners in the first half, Sts. Peter & Paul (11-5) was held scoreless in the first half by a conference opponent for the first time all year, as Gunston junior standout Layla Kent seemed to be everywhere at once.
"The stress was really high," Stepp said. "We do a prayer before every single game. Then we came together (at halftime) and we prayed again."
The Sabres earned three more corners in the first seven minutes of the third quarter, but couldn't dent the scoreboard. But SSPP made its fourth corner of the period count, as Webb unloaded a sweeping drive that buzzed by Herons goalie Loreli deGour with 6:52 remaining in the third period for a 1-0 lead.
"It was a reverse chip," Webb said. "I saw the (defender) where she was, and I knew I had to pull around her. So I just pulled it to the left and just took the shot. I was aiming for the corner. I was just happy to get the corner in."
Just 55 seconds into the fourth quarter though, Gunston (9-4) pieced together a concerted push that got behind SSPP goalie Pyper Mister and finished with Kate Zottarelli's goal into the left side of the cage.
"We've been working so much more on our mental game this season, and we've had so many more games," Gunston assistant Jen Matthews said. "It's just given us a lot more opportunities to connect as a team, work as a team. We really peaked at the right time of the season."
Webb though struck again with 5:18 remaining.
"I knew we needed a goal," Webb said. "I didn't want to go into overtime. I knew we needed to get a goal and I just felt the adrenaline rush of wanting to score. Just took a shot when I needed to. We worked well as a team to get it off."
Gunston got tagged with a 2-minute card with just under 4 minutes remaining, and the Sabres capitalized, as Webb sent a smash toward the goal that Stepp — in a move that looked like an act of self defense — made a beautiful deflection for a 3-1 lead.
"I was so surreal, because Angie cranked a shot off from the top and it was up in the air," Stepp said. "I didn't hear a whistle so at first I thought it was a corner. But she ripped the shot off and it was coming at me so my initial reaction was hit at the ball in some way, shape of form. And it just deflected off right into the goal. It was amazing. I've never done that in my whole career, and it was just perfect to have it happen in our championship game."
Despite losing to the Sabres for a third straight year, Matthews and Gunston head coach Yvonne Gazelle gushed over their team's play.
"They did amazing," said Gazelle, who in addition to Kent's outstanding all-around play, got a big effort from Grace Shepherd, who is bound for Central Michigan University. "I'm super proud of these girls."
It was Sts. Peter & Paul's fourth championship in five years.
"The last two goals were simply amazing," McQuaid said. "Happy for Jules and Angie; the finish."
McQuaid acknowledged her past two championship teams had a tendency to lean heavily on Webb's older sister, Gennie Webb, now playing for Virginia Commonwealth University.
"It was not just one person; we relied on her a lot," McQuaid said of Gennie Webb. "This year I have a group of girls, who played as a unit and supported each other. And they were fabulous."
Notes: Kent was named the ESIAC player of the year, and along with teammates Grace Shepherd, Gabi Shepherd and Izzy Labrador, was named to the all-ESIAC first-team. … Sts. Peter & Paul's Webb, Stepp, Reagan Wolters, Lucy Rankin, Kat Murphy, and Claire Bieber all earned first-team honors. SSPP's Caroline Corson was an honorable mention pick.

title: Orrell nets equalizer, game-winner to lift Easton over Rams in double overtime
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Orrell nets equalizer, game-winner to lift Easton over Rams in double overtime

 October 24, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 614
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY — It was a Warrior's cry."The story's not done," declared a member of Easton High's field hockey team before breaking the pregame huddle.
The Warriors did indeed extend their 2024 story Thursday afternoon. And as usual — at least when it comes to chapters with big games — they needed more than the usual amount of time to finish and deliver a happy ending.
Olivia Orrell scored the equalizer late in the fourth period, then knocked in the game-winner 1 minute, 52 seconds into the second overtime yesterday, lifting Easton to a 2-1 victory over No. 2 seed Parkside in a Class 2A East II semifinal.
Winners of six straight, the third-seeded Warriors (10-3) advance to Tuesday's 2A East II final at top-seeded Stephen Decatur (11-3).
"These girls never give up," said Easton head coach Kim Neff, whose team has played beyond regulation four times this season, losing a shootout to two-time Bayside champion Queen Anne's and beating perennial conference heavyweights Pocomoke and Kent Island in OT before yesterday's double-overtime thriller. "And as exhausted as they were, they never ever give up."
But Easton could have.
After a scoreless first half, the Warriors earned four penalty corners in the third period but couldn't beat Rams goalie Eden Hirsch. Easton continued applying pressure.
Then with 7:20 left in regulation, Parkside's Ava Holland converted a pass from Mady Bleile for a 1-0 Rams lead.
Neff immediately called time.
"I called time because I knew they were going to get in their own heads with that goal," Neff said of her team. "I knew I had to bring them back together as as unit and tell them we had seven minutes (in regulation). That's plenty of time to score and get ahead. And sure enough, they took that and within three minutes they were able to put one in the goal."
Easton surged into the circle and earned another corner. Hirsch made an initial save on the play. But Ryan Quicke gained possession and got the ball to Orrell, who tucked into the right corner of the cage with 3:52 remaining in regulation.
"When they scored the first goal, it put a drive in us to like dig deep," Orrell said. "Coach said we had it and she knew we had the energy. We just had the discipline. And the discipline I think as a team really got us through the game."
Easton's defense kept it a 1-1 tie through the first 10-minute overtime.
Freshman goalie Taylor Bowen (five saves) kicked away a sweeping backhand from Bleile 1:05 into the extra session. The Rams earned back-to-back corners but were denied, with Addie Knox making a clear on the second corner. Easton's Bis Johnson then swept away a ball inches from the goal line with 2 minutes remaining.
Hirsch answered, making a big save just 15 seconds later, forcing the game into a second OT.
The Warriors got two corners early, and capitalized on the second, as Orrell continuously hit at the ball before sneaking it into the back of the cage for the winner.
"Too many," Orrell answered when asked how many times she hit the ball before scoring. "We were really determined. We just got it in. It was great."
The Rams, who shut out Easton earlier in the season, finish 9-4.
"I think it was a great game from both sides," Parkside head coach Stephanie Cason said. "It just didn't fall in our favor."
KENT ISLAND 4 NORTH CAROLINE 0
STEVENSVILLE — Willow Yost scored two goals and set up a third as second-seeded Kent Island blanked the No. 3 seed Bulldogs.
The second-seeded Buccaneers (9-3-1) played at top-seed Queen Anne's (11-1-1) in the region final on Tuesday.
Ellie Burnside and Parker Tengwall each scored once for Kent Island. Goalie Brynja Petursson made seven saves.

title: Warriors beat clock, Seahawks
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors beat clock, Seahawks

 October 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 675
 Words 

 Read News Document

 It's won on a penalty stroke in overtime.It's also won on penalty corners — once in overtime, once in double OT.
Tuesday evening, Easton High's field hockey team found yet another way to win — and fray their coaches nerves — scoring just before the clock ran dry.
Addie Knox scored on a corner with 11 seconds remaining in regulation, boosting the Warriors to a 2-1 victory over top-seeded Stephen Decatur in the Class 2A East Region II championship in Berlin.
Easton (11-3), which has won seven straight, is seeded fourth in the Class 2A state tournament and will host fifth-seeded Hereford (11-3) on Thursday at 3 p.m. in a quarterfinal match.
"They never give up," Easton head coach Kim Neff said of her team during a phone interview Wednesday. "They never come off the field thinking like, 'We're done.'"
Decatur (11-4) took a 1-0 lead in the second quarter on Jill Burton's goal, and carried that lead into halftime. But the Warriors didn't panic.
"I feel like this is our MO really," Neff said. "We're used to coming from behind. We don't stress too much about it. We knew we had plenty of time to get back in that game. And I told them, 'Just go put a goal in right now and score and tie it up.' And sure enough they went and tied it up."
Less than 2 minutes into the second half, Easton's Myka Motovidlak smacked a drive toward the goal that was knocked into the cage by Georgia Spies for a 1-1 tie.
"We have faced a lot of challenges this season," Neff said. "Not a lot of teams have. Some teams it comes a little easier to win. I feel running into the playoffs that's an advantage for us. We know we can come from behind. We know we can go to double overtime and win. We've experienced that. I feel like that's an advantage for us."
Play evened out through the rest of the third quarter. The Seahawks then got a string of corners in the fourth quarter, but could not get anything else past Easton's defense of Bis Johnson, Kadence McGuckin, Lea Boutte and freshman goalie Taylor Bowen (12 saves).
"Our goalie saved the day," Neff said of Bowen, whose only experience in goal prior to this season was in rec league play. "Taylor just did a phenomenal job. She's so coachable and she sees the field. And she's so athletic. She just impressed all of us."
Easton survived Decatur's flurry of corners and worked the ball back into the Seahawks end with about 2 minutes remaining. It was then that Neff turned to assistant Katie Spies and said they needed to start thinking about who they were going to put on the field for the first overtime period.
But with a little under a minute to play, Easton's Ryan Quicke drew a foul, setting up a corner.
"We got in a little huddle right before we got the corner and Stella (Kabler) was like, 'This is it guys,'" Knox said. "Then I looked up at the scoreboard and it said 50 seconds left. And when (Neff) called that Liv (Olivia Orrell) was taking the direct shot, I was like, 'This is it.' Because Liv always gets it in there."
Knox inserted the ball off the end line, then moved to the left post. Orrell sent a drive that was stopped by Decatur's goalie. But the ball bounced upward toward Knox, who batted the ball into the cage for a 2-1 Warriors lead.
"It was great," Knox said. "Everybody just jumped up. I couldn't even breath."
But while Easton's players were celebrating, Neff was pleading.
"Everybody was losing their mind except me who was saying, 'We still have 11 seconds left,'" Neff said. "'Do not let them go down and get in the circle.'"
Decatur rushed downfield and got close to the circle before Johnson swept the ball out of bounds, leaving the Seahawks not enough time to retrieve the ball and mount one last threat.
"They believe in themselves and they believe in their teammates," Neff said. "It's really an awesome group of girls."

title: One is enough for Queen Anne's
author: Bill Haufe
content:
One is enough for Queen Anne's

 October 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 711
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Neither one needed a lesson on the importance of scoring first."The first team that scores is more likely to win than the second," Kent Island High head field hockey coach Laura Harding said.
"Getting that early goal, it sets the tone," Queen Anne's County head coach Shana Corder said. "And I knew going into this game, I knew both teams were going to come out to win it in regulation."
Queen Anne's and Kent Island played to a scoreless, double-overtime tie Oct. 19 before each team scored twice in a shootout in their regular-season finale.
It didn't take that long Tuesday afternoon.
Haley Cole's goal on a corner just 7 minutes in proved enough, as the Lions blanked Kent Island, 1-0, for their second straight Class 2A East Region I championship.
Queen Anne's (12-1-1) is seeded third in the 2A state tournament and will host No. 6 seed Centenniel (11-3) on Thursday at 4 p.m. in a quarterfinal.
"We're successful on our corners because our defense is so amazing," said Corder, whose team has won back-to-back Bayside Conference and regional titles for the first time in the program's history. "And it pays off for us. And all you need is one to go in. And honestly going forward, this is how the state tournament's going to go. One goal is going to get it."
One goal was all that was needed on this beautiful autumn afternoon.
Queen Anne's earned two corners in the game's first 5 minutes, then got a third with 7:20 remaining in the first quarter. Jordan Bilbo sent an entry pass to Ellee McLean, who quickly sent the ball back Bilbo. Positioned to the right of the goal, Bilbo centered a pass to an unmarked Cole about five yards from the cage. Cole didn't hesitate, quickly sweeping shot under the lunge of Bucs goalie Brynja Petursson and into the left side of the cage for a 1-0 lead.
"We've been working really hard on corner execution, and every practice it's been getting better and better," Cole said. "And I got the perfect pass from Jordan and happened to be the one. It was really a team effort. We were all in there to get it done and earn the corner. I just happened to be the one lucky to tap it in."
That was plenty for Queen Anne's defense.
Since yielding a goal to Crisfield on Oct. 7, the Lions haven't surrendered a goal over their last six games — not counting the 1 vs. 1 against the Bucs in the regular-season finale. Corder again played Cassidy Alexander (four saves) and Caroline Kimball (two saves) two quarters each Tuesday. And even though Sydnie Harris — one of the new mainstays on a rebuilt defense — was not 100%, she played tough minutes along with linemates Sydnee Carr and Mel Gill. Corder dropped forward Aly Edwards back on defense when Harris needed a breather.
"I just knew if we scored first I knew we could do it because my defense is amazing, and they're peaking," Corder said of a unit that has now logged 10 shutouts this season. "They are peaking right now. They've done well all season.
"I had to put one of my forwards back to defense," Corder said of Edwards. "But the kids listen to what we tell them in practice and they know everybody's role. So we're just able to be successful even being sick. I'm super proud of the girls."
Harding was also proud of her defense, which limited an opponent to one goal or less for the 11th time this season. Petursson made seven saves, including a stop McLean's penalty stroke with 7:45 left in the second quarter, and made another save when the Bucs were down a man for 2 minutes in the third quarter.
"We made the save and we battled back on all the corners down here in the first half," said Harding, whose team stopped Queen Anne's on 10 of its 11 corners.
Kent Island (9-4-1) almost pulled even with 2:50 remaining, when a drive in the circle missed connecting with Ellie Burnside at the post.
"They have a good defense," Harding said of Queen Anne's. "And they've got a great goalie. It's going to be a big battle again next year, too. I think we'll be right back here again next year."

title: QA’s, Easton hoping for a Shore thing
author: Bill Haufe
content:
QA’s, Easton hoping for a Shore thing

 November 5, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 841
 Words 

 Read News Document

 They battled each other in one of the season's more memorable duels, playing 80 scoreless minutes before settling things in 1v1s.That was Oct. 1, when Queen Anne's County High's field hockey team outlasted Easton in a shootout, part of a 14-game Lions' unbeaten streak.
The Warriors have not lost since that clash, reeling off eight straight victories.
Wednesday, 36 days later after that marathon, Queen Anne's and Easton prepare to play in the Class 2A state semifinals at Glen Burnie High School, not against each other, but hoping to possibly create the first all-Eastern Shore state final since 1997.
"How great would it be?" Queen Anne's longtime head coach Shana Corder asked rhetorically. "I am rooting for Easton and Queen Anne's to win this one. I think that would be an awesome setup."
Warrior head coach Kim Neff seconded that notion.
"That would be so wild," Neff said of an all-Shore final that hasn't happened since Pocomoke defeated Kent County in the 1997 Class 1A championship. "That would be so cool."
Of course, Corder and Neff each know that dream match doesn't happen unless their respective teams get past a pair of unbeatens tonight.
Third-seeded Queen Anne's (13-1-1) goes first, when it plays three-time defending state champion and No. 2 seed Glenelg (15-0) at 5:30 p.m. Fourth-seeded Easton (12-3) follows in a meeting with No. 1 seed Manchester Valley (15-0) at 7:30 p.m.
"OK. So we're not undefeated," Corder said. "We're the underdog."
The Lions may have thought they would be wearing that underdog tag through at least part of this season after graduating a number of standouts off last year's 15-1 team that posted 14 shutouts and reached the state semifinals. Corder honestly thought this would be a rebuild season, since the entire defense from a year ago — with the exception of goalie Cassidy Alexander — was gone.
But after a season-opening loss at Pocomoke, Corder changed her position.
"I think they felt, 'Oh, we're not going to be as good,'" Corder said. "'We are not as good as this team.' But I was like, 'We are as good. You can't set yourself up to think you're a failure.' I think losing that game was the best blessing we've gotten all year.
"I saw their faces and they weren't used to losing, all my returners," Corder continued. "And I felt like they didn't like to lose. So I thought that gave them the drive to want to win. I felt that was our turning point."
Since then the Lions, behind their one-two goalie punch of Caroline Kimball and Alexander, and a rebuilt defense, have gone unbeaten, which included winning their second straight Bayside Conference and regional championships — a first in program history — and recording 11 shutouts.
"I feel every team we play has given us their best game because we did so well (last year)," Corder said. "They understand pressure. They've been here before. All the returners know what this feels like. Hopefully they already felt the pressure. We've had 1v1 games, overtime, blah, blah, blah. I'm just hoping they are able to rise to the occasion Wednesday."
Though Easton didn't have a 2023 season that compared to Queen Anne's, Neff was filled with optimism at the outset of this season.
"I knew we were capable of getting this far," Neff said. "A lot of these girls I've coached since they were in kindergarten, and I know their potential. It was the most athletic group that I have seen (during preseason tryouts). I think them playing some travel ball together and being on rec teams together, they know each other well, which helps."
But Easton's record was sitting at 4-3 after the 1v1 loss to Queen Anne's. The Warriors moved to 5-3 with a shutout of Kent County.
Then came a 3-2 overtime victory over Pocomoke.
"We have a long history with Pocomoke," Neff said. "And Pocomoke tends to get the victories. So I think that game, and going into overtime, and doing what they did really solidified them. Like I knew and I had the confidence in them. But I think it solidified the confidence in them, like, 'We can do this.'"
Since that victory, Easton has defeated perennial Bayside heavyweight Kent Island 1-0 in overtime. The Warriors defeated Parkside 2-1 in overtime in a 2A East Region II semifinal, then beat Stephen Decatur 2-1 with 11 seconds remaining in regulation in the region final. Easton continued its trend for the dramatic last Thursday, defeating Hereford in a 1v1 in a state quarterfinal, placing the Warriors in the state semifinals for the first time since 2021.
"I told them, 'You've earned your spot there,'" Neff said. "'We're all good teams. We made it to the top four. We're not looking at records because every day's a clean slate for every team. We haven't seen them (Manchester Valley). They haven't seen us. And so we're going in and we're playing our game. They're ready."
Notes: Wednesday's winners will meet for the state final on Saturday at Stevenson University at 11 a.m.. … Third-seeded Pocomoke plays No. 2 seed Fallston Wednesday in a 1A state semifinal at Crofton High.

title: Top-sdded Mavs oust Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Top-sdded Mavs oust Easton

 November 7, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 650
 Words 

 Read News Document

 GLEN BURNIE — It had found multiple ways to win since early October.Easton High's field hockey team had won in overtime and double overtime. It had won with 11 seconds remaining in regulation. It had won on a penalty stroke and in a 1v1. And it continued to find paths to victory no matter how big the game.
But Wednesday night against top-seeded Manchester Valley, the Warrior offense rarely found its way into the circle and had its storybook season ended in a 3-0 loss to the Mavericks in a Class 2A state semifinal at Glen Burnie High School's Pop Whayland Stadium.
Manchester Valley (16-0) advances to Saturday's 11 a.m. Class 2A state championship game where it will meet three-time defending state champion Glenelg (16-0) at Stevenson University's Mustang Stadium.
"I'm so proud of them," said Easton head coach Kim Neff, whose team had its eight-game win streak ended, finishing the year at 12-4. "Taylor Bowen again had so many shots on her that she was able to save. They battled many corners clear. It was a defensive-heavy game and they handled it very well."
Indeed, the Mavericks, who had blanked their previous three playoff opponents by a combined 27-0, were held to their lowest goal total of the postseason.
"Their whole team, they played hard," Manchester Valley head coach Denean Koontz said. "They did a very nice job of doubling us. They took us out of our game plan a little bit. They stepped to the ball very well. Defensively, they were on us everywhere. They did a very nice job of smothering the ball and smothering our players."
The Mavericks finished with 11 corners before Easton earned its first with only 1 minute, 26 seconds remaining in the game.
By then the No. 1 seed had already built a three-goal cushion that was started off a pair of first-quarter corners.
Bowen, Easton's freshman goalie, and her defense weathered Manchester Valley's first two corners in the opening 5 minutes. The Mavericks were awarded their third corner less than 3 minutes later and converted, as Lily Brookhart scored off Shelby Wurzburger's assist for a 1-0 lead.
Manchester Valley earned its fifth corner with 13 seconds remaining in the first quarter, and again capitalized, with Allie Largent setting up Brookhart's second goal with no time showing on the clock.
"They were aggressive," Neff said of Manchester Valley, which held Easton scoreless for the first time since a 1v1 loss to Queen Anne's on Oct. 1. "And their stick skills were incredible."
Bowen made a save on the Mavs' first corner of the second period, and watched her teammates foil a second corner near the end of the period.
But Easton generated little offense, the long rushes downfield by Olivia Orrell and Addie Knox were often and quickly stopped well short of the circle.
"I do feel like my girls held their own," Neff said. "And I think this is where it really comes into play not having a turf field, and not being able to practice on a turf field, and play on a turf field. It's hard to keep up with the competition. Their whole team was just fast."
Manchester Valley picked up three more corner chances in the third, but could not add to its lead as Bowen registered two more saves on corners.
"Our defense, our middies, they all stepped up," Neff said. "I will say I feel like each quarter we came out a little more aggressive cutting to the ball better. I feel if we had one more quarter you might have seen maybe a goal."
Manchester Valley put away one more goal with only 4 seconds left on the third-quarter clock, when Carroll County scoring leader Amanda Herrold scored on a breakaway.
Though they continued battling, the Warriors mounted few threats and got their first corners in succession with 1:26 left, when Mavericks' goalie Makayla Shoaf registered her lone save.
"They played hard," Koontz said of Easton. "They did a great job."
